title: Why 96% of Creators Don't Make a Living
summary: Vendor article: only a few percent of creators earn a living because brand deals and ad share are rented income; pitches subscription apps as the fix.

assertions.quote: 46% of full-time creators earn less than $1,000 a year, while only 12% make more than $50,000
Every one of these resets to zero the day a creator stops posting.

verdicts.note: Platform ad revenue tracks views and brand deals are per-campaign; back-catalogue income exists but is small for most.

assertions.quote: The creators who make a real living almost all run a product that charges money every month

verdicts.note: Subscriptions and products are a growing share, but surveys still show brand deals dominate top-creator income; this is a vendor pitch.
Creator surveys show brand deals remain the largest income source for most full-time creators, and the claim comes from a vendor.

assertions.quote: A creator with 50,000 engaged followers and a $10 monthly app can out-earn a creator with 2 million passive followers
It is a lottery with 50 million tickets and a handful of winners.
brand deals account for roughly 70% of creator revenue

verdicts.note: Goldman Sachs estimates about seventy percent from brand deals; the volatility claim is reasonable but not measured.
